name: EUWC World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The EUWC World Heavyweight Championship is the fed's flagship title, first won by STEALTH at Summer Sizzler on 28 July 1996 — the same week EUWC's own Ultra Brawl series began. The belt changed hands rapidly through its founding two years — Fred Rogers, Don Hall (three times), Genesis Taylor, Dan Sokolov, X.Plosion, HICAL (twice), YAHOO and Chet Jenkins all held it before HICAL's own refusal to defend it at When Worlds Collide helped trigger EUWC's first hiatus in April 1998. HICAL, STEALTH, Dan Sokolov and Erik Kelly kept it moving through the fed's second era, into a run of short reigns (Ray Santana, Triple T and Neighborhood Sniper trading it four times inside two months in 2000) before David Harten's win, at the same show the ledger bills "Caged In!," carried it into a second hiatus that November. Cuchulain, Jordan Lockhart, Buck Naked, STEALTH and Rob Sampson cycled it through a third short era before a third hiatus in June 2002; Jordan Lockhart's second reign reopened it in April 2003, and Paul Doom, Lord Alucard, Angel of Death, Jay Smash, Holocaust (twice), Damian Stone, Danny Collins, Sean Taylor and Stephen Greer carried it across a fourth hiatus the fed's own ledger buries inside Sean Taylor's own 2004–2005 reign, deducting 220 days from its recorded length rather than pretending the promotion never went dark. STEALTH carried it across several further reigns spanning more than a decade, the last coming at the 4th Annual Chad Dupree Memorial Cup on 28 October 2007, a sixteen-man tournament held after the belt was declared vacant amid the chaos that followed Ultra Brawl IX. Through 2006 and 2007 the belt changed hands rapidly among the fed's own later roster — Jay Smash three times, Adam Benjamin, Nero and "Classy" Mike C among them — before STEALTH's own final win closed out the surviving ledger.

name: EUWC World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The EUWC World Tag Team Championship's own ledger opens with the Specialists (Nate Augustine & Roger Thorpe) on 28 July 1996, the same Summer Sizzler card that crowned the fed's first World Heavyweight Champion, and changed hands more than a dozen times across the founding two years — the Beantown Bruisers, the Outsiders, the Black Panthers (twice each), the Surf Patrol, the Glamour Boys (twice), the Hellraisers, Team PSD and Harlem Connection among the teams — with three separate vacancies along the way (a controversial finish, the Outsiders' own contract lapsing, the Black Panthers' retirement) before Harlem Connection's reign carried it into EUWC's first hiatus in April 1998. Team PSD's own second reign reopened it in October 1999, and a run of ad hoc pairings and named teams — the Salvation, the Dark Angels, the Kool Klub, American Mafia, the Blood Brothers, Alliance of Violence, the Kings, Extreme Lightning and the Wannabes among them — carried it through EUWC's second era into its second hiatus. New Pimps on the Block reopened it in September 2001; Diabolic Forces, the Enders, the Motley Crew and a returning American Mafia carried it through the third era before a third hiatus. Nero & Big G (billed under Lynch Garrisson's own tag-team nickname "Big G") won it three separate times across the fourth era, trading it with Scott Samson & T-Charger, the Action Faction, Buck Naked & Samuel Roundtree, the Dream Team (twice), Shock Therapy, the Dominion (twice), U.S. Express, the Rebellion and Diabolic Forces, before Team Danger's own reign absorbed a fourth hiatus (240 days deducted).

name: EUWC International Championship
epitaph: The EUWC International Championship's own history table opens with Ahmed the Powerhouse winning a tournament final the night EUWC opened, 28 July 1996, and changed hands some fifteen times through the fed's founding two years — X.Plosion, Don Hall, The Crow, Consequence, HICAL and Dan Sokolov (twice) among the holders — before Dan Sokolov's own vacating reign carried it into EUWC's first hiatus in April 1998. Mid-lineage, on 28 September 1997, HICAL unified the North American Championship into this belt. Fred Rogers, Dan Sokolov, Triple T, Erik Kelly, Ray Santana, Cuchulain, The Chameleon, Kritical Kondition and STEALTH carried the title through its second era; Sledgehammer, T-Charger, Simon, HICAL, Larry Serson, Triple T, Neighborhood Sniper, Gavin Glass, David Harten and Virus carried it through the third, before a third hiatus vacated it in June 2002. Nick Marshall, Damian Stone, Cole Justice, Sean Taylor, Jim Roberts, Apocalypse, Danny Collins and Lynch Garrisson cycled it through the fourth era — Apocalypse's own loss to Danny Collins staged at a show the Uprising event-history page dates a full year earlier than the title ledger itself, an unresolved discrepancy between the fed's own documents — before Sean Taylor's second reign absorbed a fourth hiatus (230 days deducted) and Tyrone Walker reopened it at Superiority II in July 2005. After a run the fed's own record does not otherwise explain, the ledger resumes in the mid-2000s with Rocko Daymon, Hawkeye (twice), Sevyn, Jonathan Darkstar and Cobris Grayson carrying it through EUWC's final fwrestling.com-hosted years.

name: EUWC North American Championship
epitaph: The EUWC North American Championship's own history table opens with STEALTH winning it in EUWC's first-ever 20-man Blood Bath, 27 October 1996, then changed hands seven more times across the fed's founding year before Chet Jenkins carried it into a unification match at And The Winner Is... Part V: War Games on 28 September 1997, where HICAL (as International Champion) absorbed it into the International Championship. The belt itself lay dormant for eight years — the ledger's own "Defunct" — before Lt. Hawkeye's win over Cuchulain and Tony DeLucci at Blood Bath, 20 November 2005, "resurrected thanks to the roster split"; due to a short hiatus that same night, the reign's own active clock is recorded as beginning 9 February 2006. Angel of Death, Cuchulain, Artur Arina and Braden Kincaid carried it into the fed's own final active years. Braden Kincaid's own reign carried the belt to its second and final unification, into the EUWC International Championship, in the Unification Match at Blood Bath, 9 July 2008 -- Kincaid himself was never pinned in the fall.

events.title: euwc-international
events.note: HICAL (International Champion) defeated Chet Jenkins (North American Champion) at And The Winner Is... Part V: War Games to unify the belts. The North American title lay dormant until a November 2005 revival.

events.title: euwc-international
events.note: Cobris Grayson (entering as European Champion) defeated Braden Kincaid (North American Champion, among others) in a four-way Unification Match at Blood Bath to become International Champion and unify the belts.

name: EUWC United States Championship
epitaph: The EUWC United States Championship changed hands more often than any other EUWC belt on record. Its ledger opens with YAHOO winning a tournament final on 25 May 1997 and cycled rapidly through Don Hall, The Crow, Stephon Kardell and Kris Blade before the promotion's first hiatus in April 1998; once EUWC returned it kept the same pace, naming dozens of reigns across every era through the promotion's second hiatus (Angel of Death, Ray Santana and Tony DeLucci among the early holders), its third (Cuchulain, T-Rex, David Harten and Bibyl), its fourth (Larry Serson, Rob Sampson, Gavin Glass, Marshall Snow and Virus), and its fifth (Ryan Baker, Samuel Roundtree, Major Action, T-Charger and Scott Samson) — Samuel Roundtree's second reign, in June 2005, absorbing the EUWC 52 Wild Championship outright in a fatal four way Unification match. Angel of Death carried the belt three separate times; Adam Benjamin lost the belt off-page, exact date unrecorded, to Texas Lightning, who carried it into the title's own final unification, into the EUWC International Championship, in the Unification Match at Blood Bath, 9 July 2008.

events.title: euwc-international
events.note: Cobris Grayson (entering as European Champion) defeated Texas Lightning (United States Champion, among others) in a four-way Unification Match at Blood Bath to become International Champion and unify the belts.

name: EUWC European Championship
epitaph: The EUWC European Championship's own ledger opens in July 2004 with Jack "The Ripper," whose two reigns both came against opponents billed from a partner promotion, RBW — one of the clearest surviving traces of EUWC's own cross-federation booking. The Monster, Jacob Jacobs, Apocalypse, T. Waring and the Odinist cycled the belt through RBW-billed defenses before the Odinist's own retirement, when the RBW itself closed, vacated it in August 2005; T. Waring's second reign, the Monster's second, and John Doe carried it into the fed's short fifth-era hiatus around Blood Bath 2005. Chris Comet's 460-day reign, the longest recorded on the belt, ran from June 2006 to Ultra Brawl IX in September 2007, when Cobris Grayson won it. Grayson's own reign carried the belt to its own unification, into the EUWC International Championship (his own second title), in the Unification Match at Blood Bath, 9 July 2008.

events.title: euwc-international
events.note: Cobris Grayson, the reigning European Champion, won this four-way Unification Match at Blood Bath to become International Champion, folding the European title he already held into the International title he won in the same match.

name: EUWC World Juniorweight Championship
epitaph: Discovered only through EUWC’s full-card event-history pages rather than any dedicated ledger: the Perfect Pugilest regained it at Ultra Brawl in August 1996, Sweet Daddy Bad Ass regained it again that October at EUWC’s first Blood Bath, Michael Foreman won it fresh at Ultra Brawl II in August 1997, and Ender won a Four Corners match for it at Blood Bath 1997. The fed’s own text names it inconsistently, sometimes "Juniorweight Championship" and sometimes "World Juniorweight Championship" — the same belt, one lineage.
notes: Every reign recovered from the Ultra Brawl and Bloodbath/Blood Bath event-history pages (/promotions/euwc/archive/ultrabrawl9-ultrabrawl-history.html, /promotions/euwc/archive/bloodbath2007-bloodbath-history.html); no dedicated title-history ledger page survives for this belt.

name: EUWC International Tag Team Championship
aka: EUWC Unified International Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Killers Inc retained it at Ultra Brawl in August 1996 over the Missouri Connection, then apparently lost it — unrecorded — to Badd Company before that October’s Blood Bath, where Badd Company retained over a team the card spells "Kiillers Incorprated." At Ultra Brawl II the following August the Midnight Massacre won it from Cause & Effect in a "Unification Match," becoming, per the card’s own words, the "Unified International Tag Team Champions."
notes: Every reign recovered from the Ultra Brawl and Bloodbath/Blood Bath event-history pages; no dedicated title-history ledger page survives for this belt. Only reigns with a recorded WIN are structured (Killers Inc’s and Badd Company’s "retain" defenses are recorded as matches, not reign rows, since no won-date survives for either).

name: EUWC North American Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Powers of Destruction won it from Cuttz ’n’ Broozis at EUWC’s first Blood Bath, 27 October 1996 — the only reign the surviving record attests.
notes: Recovered from the Bloodbath/Blood Bath event-history page; no dedicated title-history ledger page survives for this belt.

name: EUWC Hardcore Television Championship
epitaph: Albino won the title’s debut match, a Caribbean Strap Match over the Wraith, at Blood Bath 1997 — the only reign the surviving record attests. Distinct from the plain "Television Championship" John Shaft held the year before, and from the later "Hardcore Championship" that debuts after EUWC’s first hiatus.
notes: Recovered from the Bloodbath/Blood Bath event-history page; no dedicated title-history ledger page survives for this belt.

name: EUWC Television Championship
epitaph: John Shaft retained it against Consequence by disqualification at EUWC’s first Blood Bath, 27 October 1996 — the only appearance the surviving record attests, and no won-date for John Shaft’s own reign survives. Distinct from the "Hardcore Television Championship" Albino wins the following year.
notes: Recovered from the Bloodbath/Blood Bath event-history page; no dedicated title-history ledger page survives for this belt.

name: EUWC Hardcore Championship
epitaph: The EUWC Hardcore Championship is attested only through the Ultra Brawl, Bloodbath and Aftershock event-history pages — no dedicated title-history ledger for it survives, and several hand-offs between its eight recorded reigns are unrecorded gaps rather than invented continuity. Neighborhood Sniper won it in a Ladder Match at Ultra Brawl III in October 1999; T-Charger, Johnny Hardcore, Kaine, Marshall Snow, Sevyn and Bibyl carried it in turn across the fed's second, third and fourth eras, the title going dark for stretches the surviving record never explains. Bibyl's win over Sevyn at Blood Bath, 30 November 2003, is the last EUWC Hardcore Championship reign attested anywhere in the held record. Distinct from the 1997 EUWC Hardcore Television Championship, a separate, one-match-only belt from the fed's founding era.
notes: Minted entirely from event-history mentions (no dedicated title-history ledger page survives for this belt); several reigns carry an honest gap where the actual title change is unattested.

name: EUWC 52 Wild Championship
epitaph: The EUWC 52 Wild Championship is attested only through the Uprising, Superiority, Aftershock, Ultra Brawl and Bloodbath event-history pages — no dedicated title-history ledger for it survives. "Brooklyn's Finest" Kai A.
notes: Minted entirely from event-history mentions (no dedicated title-history ledger page survives for this belt).

events.title: euwc-unitedstates
events.note: Samuel Roundtree won a fatal four way over Havoc, "All Business" Eric McRae & "Classy" Mike C (the reigning 52 Wild Champion) at Main Frame, unifying the 52 Wild Championship into the United States Championship.

name: EUWC Tag Team Championship
epitaph: A Main-Frame-exclusive title founded via a Tag Team Turmoil match at Ultra Brawl VIII (24 September 2006), announced by Matt Pickstock as a second tag lineage alongside the existing EUWC World Tag Team Championship -- the Turmoil's own match text does not survive, but the Black Death Gauntlet are confirmed the founding champions by the very next show read.
notes: Minted from a confirmed-champion billing (chad-dupree-memorial-cup-2006-10-15) plus Matt Pickstock's own prior announcement (main-frame-2006-08-20/09-19); the founding match itself is unattested.

name: EUWC Championship
epitaph: Blackout's own world title, distinct from Main Frame's EUWC World Heavyweight Championship -- Cuchulain is confirmed champion by Ultra Brawl VIII (24 September 2006) and retains it through a cross-promotional Champion vs. Champion win over Jay Smash at the 2006 Chad Dupree Memorial Cup. How or when Cuchulain won the title is not cleanly attested -- a recap on main-frame-2006-09-29 names an "EUWC Championship Tournament" dated 24 August 2006, but that recap's own text is too fragmentary and reused across clips to confirm the actual final.
notes: Minted from confirmed-champion billing; the title's own founding match is unattested (see epitaph).
